description:
## Context

`OctoPi.TUI.RenderThrottle` (`apps/octo_pi_tui/lib/octo_pi/tui/render_throttle.ex`) is a pure functional module:
- `new(opts)` — struct with `min_interval_ms: 16` (matches upstream `MIN_RENDER_INTERVAL_MS = 16`)
- `should_render?(t)` — true if elapsed ≥ min_interval or first render
- `record_render(t)` — returns updated struct with monotonic timestamp
- `metrics(t)` — returns `{render_count, skip_count}`
- `check_width_overflow(lines, width)` — ANSI-aware line width validation

Upstream embeds throttle logic directly in the TUI class (`tmp/pi-mono/packages/tui/src/tui.ts` lines 230, 472-519). The Elixir `Renderer` GenServer (`apps/octo_pi_tui/lib/octo_pi/tui/renderer.ex`) renders on every call with no rate limiting.

## Implementation steps

### 1. Read Renderer before all changes

Read `apps/octo_pi_tui/lib/octo_pi/tui/renderer.ex` in full. Understand: state struct fields, how `render/3` or equivalent is called, whether any throttling already exists.

### 2. Add throttle to Renderer state

```elixir
throttle: RenderThrottle.new()
```

Add `alias OctoPi.TUI.RenderThrottle`.

### 3. Gate render on throttle decision

In the render handler:
```elixir
if RenderThrottle.should_render?(state.throttle) do
  do_render(lines, width)
  throttle = RenderThrottle.record_render(state.throttle)
  %{state | throttle: throttle}
else
  %{state | throttle: %{state.throttle | skip_count: state.throttle.skip_count + 1}}
end
```

### 4. Add force-render bypass

Accept a `force: boolean` option on the render call. Resize events and first-render must set `force: true` to bypass the throttle. Find the resize/SIGWINCH handler in `apps/octo_pi_tui/lib/octo_pi/tui/interactive.ex` and update its render call accordingly.

### 5. Wire metrics to telemetry

```elixir
{render_count, skip_count} = RenderThrottle.metrics(throttle)
if rem(render_count, 100) == 0 do
  :telemetry.execute([:octo_pi, :tui, :renderer], %{renders: render_count, skips: skip_count}, %{})
end
```

### 6. Wire width overflow check

In `do_render/2`, call `RenderThrottle.check_width_overflow(lines, width)` and `Logger.warning/1` on overflow (should not occur in production; indicates a renderer bug).

### 7. Tests

- Rapid calls within 16ms result in increasing `skip_count`
- `force: true` bypasses throttle regardless of elapsed time
- `render_count` increments correctly after each render
- Existing Renderer tests still pass

## Notes
- Pure functional design — no `Process.send_after` or timer process needed. The decision happens at call time.
- 16ms default matches upstream exactly.
title: Integrate OctoPi.TUI.RenderThrottle into the Renderer GenServer
